_note: Golden cross-language fixtures for the lock-state contract, consumed by BOTH scripts/lock-math-test.mjs (src/shared/lock-math.ts) and the smartblocker-core cargo tests (lock_math.rs / merge.rs). Every case here must pass identically in TypeScript and Rust — that is the parity guarantee between the extension and the desktop companion. Schedule rules pinned to `tzOffsetMinutes` evaluate against that FIXED offset regardless of the host zone, so the tz-pinned cases below are host-independent by design (red-team #26); UNPINNED rules still follow the device's current zone, which the Rust runner pins to Utc and the TS runner leaves local — legacy-window behavior is therefore covered by each language's own unit tests instead of this file. The DST-residual case documents the accepted cost of fixed-offset pins: a rule pinned on winter time fires one hour off the civil clock after a DST change (the mirror has no IANA tz database — offline build constraint). The merge runner additionally asserts commutativity (merge(b,a) == expect) and idempotence (merge(expect,expect) == expect) for every case. `reasons` array order is fixed: timer, password, delay, random-text, frozen, schedule. Delay and random-text are whole-gate LWW operations: newer releases beat stale arms, newer arms beat old releases, equal stamps keep armed/reset/longer states, and legacy peers without the new fields cannot erase active gates. Merge cases carry an optional `now` (default 0): the schedule rule asks whether exactly one side is settings_locked at merge time — with fixture stamps in the small thousands, an active timer/frozen/password means locked. The password is a timestamped arm/unlock tombstone CRDT (greater passwordTs wins; a tie keeps an armed hash over a cleared one, and two armed hashes keep the lexicographically smaller); schedules are last-writer-wins EXCEPT that a locked side's list beats an unlocked peer regardless of stamps. passwordTs and schedulesUpdatedAt are clamped to `now` by sanitize (never now+maxLockMs): both order last-writer-wins merges, so forged future stamps must never be admitted. Same-id rules at equal schedule stamps resolve by a canonical content string that includes the tz pin, so two same-id rules pinned to different zones still converge deterministically.

equal timestamps union schedules sorted by id
same id at equal timestamps keeps the canonically smaller rule
all fields merge independently
a locked side's schedules survive an unlocked peer's newer write
both sides locked: the newer schedule list still wins
tz pins ride along with the winning schedule list
same id with different tz pins at equal timestamps picks the canonically smaller pin
newer break operation wins as one unit

newer active break beats an older cancellation without shortening a lock
same-stamp break cancellation wins the fail-closed tie

deriveLockStatus.name: empty state is unlocked
active timer locks settings only
expired timer derives to inactive
timer expiring exactly now is inactive (strict >)
password lock is indefinite
frozen turkey forces blocking
until is the max of active timed ends
armed password makes until indefinite even with a timer
pinned window active: 16:00 in the pinned zone (UTC+05:30) is inside 09:00–17:00 though the device clock says 10:30 UTC
tz changed after pinning: 17:30 in the pinned zone is outside — moving the device to UTC cannot sidestep a 09:00–17:00 rule
DST residual documented: a rule pinned on winter time (-300) has NOT started at 09:30 summer civil time (13:30 UTC) — fixed offsets fire one hour off across a DST change
delayed break is pending without changing timer-lock semantics
delayed break activates at its inclusive start without changing timer-lock semantics
break expires at its exclusive end while forceBlocking stays independent
armed delay waits indefinitely before the user starts unlocking
delay countdown does not masquerade as timerUntil
delay at its deadline is ready but remains locked for background release
random-text gate is indefinite and advertises its configured length
all independent lock sources derive in stable reason order
released new gates omit optional status fields

nextBoundary.name: earliest of timer and frozen wins
a pinned rule's boundary lands on the pinned zone's clock: after 17:30 IST the next start is tomorrow 09:00 IST (03:30 UTC), not anything device-local
pending break activation is the next boundary
active break re-block is the next boundary
expired break creates no future boundary
delay waiting to be started has no trusted countdown boundary
delay deadline participates in earliest-wall-time boundary selection
ready delay creates no future boundary while awaiting release
random-text gate has no wall-clock boundary

sanitizeLockState.name: empty object becomes the empty state
absurd timer is clamped to now + maxLockMs
non-numeric and non-positive untils are dropped
password must be 64 lowercase hex chars
a future schedulesUpdatedAt clamps to now, never the lock cap
a future passwordTs clamps to now
well-formed fields pass through, invalid rules are dropped
valid tz pins pass through sanitize intact
rules with invalid tz pins are dropped, valid neighbors kept
well-formed break passes sanitize with a 24h re-block cap and clamped stamps
partial break shape becomes an empty tombstone
overlong break activation interval is rejected
wrong break timestamp types are dropped without admitting a break
valid waiting delay and minimum random text sanitize with clamped gate stamps
delay deadline uses the independent forty-day cap and maximum text passes
malformed active delay drops neutrally instead of becoming a release tombstone
waiting delay without its configured duration is dropped neutrally
out-of-range random text drops neutrally instead of unlocking
stamp-only and null releases preserve their anti-resurrection tombstones
